problem: The text says "Three efficiencies are easy to mix" but then defines four quantities: internal quantum efficiency, extraction efficiency, external quantum efficiency and power efficiency. A student counting will be confused about which three are meant.
fix: Say: "Four efficiency figures are easy to mix: internal quantum efficiency, extraction efficiency, external quantum efficiency and power (wall-plug) efficiency."

problem: "Above turn-on it is almost linear" and "a current of 30 mA above turn-on" use "turn-on" for an LED, where it normally means the forward voltage (about 1 V), not a current. The reader cannot tell whether 30 mA is the total current or the current measured above a threshold, and the answer silently treats it as the total current.
fix: Write "above a few milliamperes the curve is almost linear, so P_out = (dP_out/dI)(I − I₀) with a small intercept I₀", and in Q6 say "the current above the small turn-on intercept is 30 mA, so use I = 0.030 A in P = slope × I".

problem: The list "planar, dome, surface-emitter and edge-emitter LEDs" puts planar and dome side by side with surface emitter, although a planar LED and a dome LED are both surface emitters. The categories overlap, which contradicts the figure where planar and dome sit under surface emitter.
fix: Write: "This chapter covers surface emitters (planar and dome types, including the Burrus structure) and edge emitters, then the efficiencies, I-P curve, spectrum, modulation bandwidth and temperature behaviour."

problem: The second reason is stated as the bandgap shrinking and "reducing emission at the design wavelength", which does not actually explain why the optical power falls. The power falls because a smaller bandgap gives a lower photon energy E, so each escaping photon carries less energy even at the same photon rate.
fix: Answer: "(1) Non-radiative recombination and carrier leakage rise with temperature, so internal quantum efficiency and the number of photons fall. (2) The bandgap shrinks, so each photon has lower energy E and the peak moves to a longer wavelength; both lower the optical power at the design wavelength."

problem: The text calls the Burrus LED an important higher-radiance surface emitter, but the figure leaves it out, so the two paths mentioned in the caption do not show it.
fix: Add a "Burrus (well/window)" child under Surface emitter, beside Planar and Dome.
